name: How do I know if my Los Angeles building actually needs seismic retrofitting or if it’s just a recommendation?

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my Los Angeles building actually needs seismic retrofitting or if it’s just a recommendation?

acceptedAnswer.text:
You can usually tell by the building’s age, type, and any official notices you’ve received. In Los Angeles, many pre-1980 wood and concrete buildings, especially soft-story apartments, are either required or strongly recommended to be retrofitted.

Cities like Los Angeles have identified thousands of vulnerable buildings and send owners formal compliance orders, but even buildings not on those lists can be at risk if they’re older or on weak soil. A structural engineer or retrofit contractor can confirm whether your specific structure needs work.

Key factors:
- Year built (pre-1978 wood and pre-1980–1990 concrete are higher risk)
- Soft-story features (parking or open commercial space at ground level)
- Unreinforced masonry or non-ductile concrete elements
- Any official city or county retrofit notice or ordinance number on your property

Schedule a seismic evaluation before the next code deadline or major renovation; it’s better to discover issues on your terms than after a damaging quake. A good contractor or engineer can translate city requirements into a clear yes/no and scope of work, not just a sales pitch.

A reputable local retrofit specialist will be used to reviewing LA-area notices and can quickly tell you if your building truly needs work.
acceptedAnswer.description: Check the building’s age, type, and any city notices: most pre-1978 soft-story wood apartments and older concrete or masonry buildings in LA are strong retrofit candidates. If you’ve received a compliance order, it’s mandatory; if not, a structural engineer or retrofit contractor can evaluate risk and confirm whether work is needed.
